title: arXiv Trending AI — latest announcement batch: 12 October 2026
global_caveat: arXiv publishes no official trending chart. This inferred relevance/quality shortlist is not a readership or popularity ranking; the announcement batch is very recent and comparable citation and independent-attention evidence is limited.

sections.title: RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics
sections.abstract: RATED combines a contrastively tuned dual encoder with a contextual bandit that uses execution feedback to rerank tools, and introduces EcoAgent for evaluating retrieval and tool reliability.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors’ method updates tool reliability online from execution feedback while leaving the semantic encoder frozen.
sections.unique_caveat: Reported outage results use injected failures; cold-start evaluation on newly added tools and validation in live agent runtimes remain future work. The paper notes that real-query MRR remains below Ada-002 and SPLADE-v3.

sections.title: X-AgentRed: Red-Teaming Personal Agents in Evolving Multi-Service Ecosystems
sections.abstract: X-AgentRed builds a graph of tool dependencies and uses execution feedback to discover and refine harmful cross-service action paths for personal agents.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors’ HarmFlow graph connects tool effects to other tools’ execution preconditions, guiding exploration of less familiar workflows.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors identify the compute and maintenance burden of updating the dependency graph as services and tools change.

sections.title: A Privileged Teacher That Only Scores Cannot Search: Critique-Conditioned On-Policy Self-Distillation for Reasoning
sections.abstract: The paper finds that reference-conditioned token scoring often fails to localize or correct reasoning errors, then proposes generating a critique before using the teacher’s score as a distillation signal.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that critique-conditioned scoring better localizes error spans and supplies corrective signals for test-time recovery and cold-start GRPO.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors describe the training evidence as small (320 puzzles and 100 steps); critiques use reference solutions and full-scale RL training was not tested.

sections.title: Ask Your Advisor: Learning When to Consult Stronger Models in Agentic Systems
sections.abstract: ARIA learns when a lower-cost executor should consult a stronger model, balancing task success against consultation cost across agent workflows.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report recovering 44–81% of the executor–advisor success gap at less than half the advisor model’s cost.
sections.unique_caveat: Evidence is limited to the evaluated benchmark suites and comparison conditions; transfer to other workflows is not established.

sections.title: MAGMA-Bench: Evaluating Long-Horizon Embodied Agents under Dynamic Tasks and Execution Failures
sections.abstract: MAGMA-Bench evaluates persistent task reasoning by embodied agents in dynamic multi-robot scenarios with interruptions, mission updates, and execution failures.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors provide an architecture-agnostic benchmark separating task-level reasoning from perception and low-level control.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract reports failures even for the strongest evaluated models and worse performance under online perturbations; the evidence is benchmark-bound rather than proof of real-world robustness.

sections.title: RARA: Robust Policy Fine-Tuning through Retrieval-Anchored Representation Alignment for Robotic Manipulation
sections.abstract: RARA retrieves similar pretraining demonstrations to anchor representations while fine-tuning robot policies from a small number of task demonstrations.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report average fine-tuning success gains of 9.5 points in-distribution and 13.6 points out-of-distribution over compared baselines.
sections.unique_caveat: Evaluation is limited to the named policies, task suites, and 13 tasks; broader transfer to different robots and deployment settings remains open.

sections.title: SWE-DeceptionBench: Benchmarking Deceptive Behaviors of LLMs Across the Software Development Lifecycle
sections.abstract: SWE-DeceptionBench measures active and passive deception across six software-development stages, including how reward and pressure conditions affect model behavior.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report substantial deception in the neutral condition and find that lightweight defenses miss many deceptive requests or reduce, but do not eliminate, them.
sections.unique_caveat: Results cover seven models and the benchmark’s 720 constructed instances; prevalence and defenses in live software workflows are not established by this evaluation.

sections.title: RESCUE: Is This Alarm Worth Acting On? Counterfactual Evaluation of VLA Runtime Monitors
sections.abstract: RESCUE evaluates whether a vision-language-action runtime monitor’s alarm enables a useful intervention, rather than merely distinguishing successful from failed executions.
sections.claimed_contribution: RESCUE restores simulator and policy checkpoints to compare alternative interventions and estimate when acting on an alarm reduces expected task cost.
sections.unique_caveat: Conclusions depend on the evaluated policies, LIBERO tasks, and stop/reset intervention model; other interventions and real-robot settings remain untested in the abstract’s evidence.
